project: Reconcile ACP Architecture and Public Vocabulary Documentation
description: Reconcile the architecture, public data model, event-stream guide, and still-stale packaged-service-structure planning notes with current ACP service ownership, customer vocabulary, event lifetimes, and settled D1/D2/D3 decisions without changing production behavior or generated artifacts.

context.customerAsk: Reconcile the documentation debt recorded in docs/internal/projects/acp-program/README.md section 6. Use the actual Chat Sessions, Events, and Worker Sessions service owners; add concise public definitions for Chat Session, Worker Session, Target Episode, and Turn; preserve the separation between ephemeral FactoryResponseEvent, the process-local Events stream, and the canonical Recordings Factory Event ledger; replace or explicitly supersede the third event hierarchy with the existing workers.Kind/workers.Phase vocabulary; update only stale D1/D2/D3 packaged-service-structure notes; verify the documentation; and carry delivery through actual PR merge.
context.problem: The architecture docs name obsolete or nonexistent service packages and imply a universal durable event bus, the public data model omits ACP session and episode vocabulary, the event-stream guide describes an unimplemented third hierarchy, and stale PSS checklist language contradicts settled no-storage, event-ownership, and composition decisions.
context.solution: Correct the canonical documentation surfaces to describe actual service ownership and state lifetimes, define the new customer terms and their relationships, document source-native Worker Kind/Phase observations separately from Recordings-owned Factory history, and remove or supersede only PSS statements that still contradict D1, D2, or D3. Keep the work documentation-only and verify it with focused terminology/link review and existing repository quality gates.

acceptanceCriteria: Architecture readers see pkg/services/chat_sessions, pkg/services/events, and pkg/services/worker_sessions as the actual owners, see no nonexistent Docs service, and are not told that services communicate through a universal event bus or that the Events service is a durable ledger.
The public data model defines Chat Session, Worker Session, Target Episode, and Turn and explains their relationships in customer-facing language without exposing internal Petri-net vocabulary.

Documentation consistently distinguishes FactoryResponseEvent as ephemeral invocation progress, Events as an in-memory session-scoped stream, and Recordings FactoryEvent JSONL artifacts as canonical Factory history and replay under D1 and D2.

The event-stream guide uses the existing workers.Kind and workers.Phase vocabulary for Worker observations and the separate canonical Factory Event ledger, with the old third hierarchy removed or explicitly marked superseded rather than normalized into a new model.

The canonical PSS README and its local plan/checklist contain no still-active statements that contradict D1, D2, or D3; exact referenced package paths and document links resolve, and no unrelated documentation or production/generated surface changes.
Quality gates pass: focused documentation and link review, make readme-check when applicable, typecheck, lint, and tests required by the repository/PR CI policy.

Delivery continues through implementation and review until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation is explicitly addressed, current-main and shared-file conflicts are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; an opened, approved, green, or ready-to-merge PR is not complete.

userStories.title: Present the actual service ownership and communication model
userStories.description: As a maintainer reading the architecture guide, I want the service inventory and system-flow explanations to name the real owners and communication boundaries so I can design changes against packages and lifetimes that actually exist.
acceptanceCriteria: The service inventory identifies Chat Sessions at pkg/services/chat_sessions, Events at pkg/services/events, and Worker Sessions at pkg/services/worker_sessions, with concise responsibilities aligned to current architecture.
The inventory contains no pkg/services/chat, pkg/services/event_stream, or pkg/services/docs owner and does not imply a Docs product service.
Architecture prose and diagrams show direct service operations and bounded event delivery where applicable without claiming that every service subscribes to a universal bus.

Events is described as an in-memory, session-scoped stream for ordering, cursors, subscriptions, retention, gaps, and backpressure; Recordings remains the owner of canonical Factory history, JSONL artifacts, replay, and historical projections.

Existing architecture diagrams and frontend/backend prose no longer label the process-local Events stream as the durable replay source of truth; references to canonical replay identify the Recordings Factory Event ledger.
Focused review confirms the named service paths exist and the revised prose agrees with current service ownership; no production or generated file changes.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: 2026-08-04: Reconciled docs/architecture/architecture.md with the implemented Chat Sessions, Events, Worker Sessions, and Recordings boundaries. Replaced the universal Event Bus diagrams and prose with direct service operations and bounded session-topic delivery; identified Recordings FactoryEvent JSONL artifacts as the canonical replay/history source; and corrected the frontend diagrams and prose to consume Recordings-backed Factory history. Focused owner-path/obsolete-terminology review and make typecheck pass.

userStories.title: Define ACP session and episode vocabulary in the public data model
userStories.description: As a customer or integrator, I want concise definitions for Chat Session, Worker Session, Target Episode, and Turn so I can understand how a conversation invokes a target and how its work is grouped.
acceptanceCriteria: Chat Session is defined as the customer-facing conversation/control context that can address a target and contains ordered turns, without presenting it as canonical Factory replay history.
Target Episode is defined as one bounded attempt to run or interact with a selected target within a Chat Session, and its relationship to the selected Factory or other target is explicit.
Worker Session is defined as the execution/control context for a Worker participating in a Target Episode, including the possibility of multiple Worker Sessions where orchestration requires them.
Turn is defined as one ordered user/agent interaction unit within a Chat Session and is related clearly to the Target Episode and any Worker activity it triggers.
The relationship text or diagram uses customer-facing vocabulary and preserves the internal/customer model boundary; it does not expose Petri tokens, places, transitions, or markings.
FactoryResponseEvent remains explicitly ephemeral and process-local, outside the canonical Recordings FactoryEvent replay ledger, and the surrounding definitions agree with D1 and D2.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: 2026-08-04: Added customer-facing Chat Session, Target Episode, Turn, and Worker Session definitions plus their relationship diagram to docs/architecture/data-model.md. Clarified that FactoryResponseEvent is ephemeral and process-local, outside the Recordings-owned canonical FactoryEvent replay ledger. Verified the terms against the Chat Sessions and Worker Sessions public contracts; make typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Document the two shipped event vocabularies without a third taxonomy
userStories.description: As an implementer consuming event output, I want the event-stream guide to describe the source-native Worker observation vocabulary separately from canonical Factory history so I do not implement against an invented normalized hierarchy.
acceptanceCriteria: Worker observations are described using the declared workers.Kind values SESSION, RUN, TURN, MESSAGE, REASONING, TOOL, FILE_CHANGE, PLAN, PROGRESS, USAGE, ERROR, and STREAM_GAP and workers.Phase values STARTED, DELTA, UPDATED, COMPLETED, FAILED, and CANCELED.
The guide explains that valid Kind/Phase combinations and their typed payloads are source-native Worker contracts; it does not imply that every Kind accepts every Phase.
Canonical Factory history is documented separately as Recordings-owned FactoryEvent values and JSONL artifacts used for replay and historical inspection.
The prior nested Factory/Worker/User/Agent/Tool hierarchy is removed or clearly labeled as superseded conceptual material that is not a supported contract.
The guide does not introduce a replacement normalized event taxonomy, rename shipped enum values, or conflate Events stream retention with durable Factory history.
Focused comparison against the current public Worker declarations and Recordings documentation confirms the examples and terminology are accurate; no enum, runtime, OpenAPI, or generated changes.
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Close the remaining stale PSS decision language
userStories.description: As a program planner, I want the canonical packaged-service-structure notes and their local checklist to reflect settled D1, D2, and D3 decisions so no future packet is admitted for canceled storage work or blocked behind a nonexistent composition lease.
acceptanceCriteria: Still-stale checklist or plan statements that defer Recordings-backed checkpoint storage or Recordings durable log/cursor/retention are changed to state that this work is canceled, not deferred, under D1.
PSS guidance consistently states that Recordings owns canonical Factory JSONL history and replay while Events owns only the in-memory, session-scoped stream behavior under D2.

PSS guidance consistently states that ordinary additive edits under pkg/wire, pkg/root, and pkg/initializer are shared composition surfaces resolved by normal rebase and do not create an exclusive composition lease under D3; genuine structural contract edits remain subject to explicit ownership controls.
Already-correct README/plan language is preserved rather than rewritten, and only contradictory or incomplete local checklist/plan text is reconciled.
The documentation does not reopen checkpoint APIs, add storage-engine work, alter PSS packet implementation scope, or schedule L4 Worker control work.
Focused link and terminology review plus make readme-check pass where applicable, and the diff remains limited to the requested documentation and task artifacts.
Typecheck passes
